taxximizer.assume.1: You live in Israel and run everything from there, so a US company is Israeli-resident for tax too. No US office, staff or inventory (no US-connected income).
taxximizer.assume.2: Company and C-corp profits are all paid out this year (salary, then dividend). Leaving profit inside defers the dividend tax, but from 2025 retained profits above ₪750k can cost 2% a year (§81ב).
taxximizer.assume.3: §62א isn't applied: a one-person service company can have its profit taxed as your salary (if 70%+ comes from one client, or from 2025 once it holds over ₪750k of profit).
taxximizer.assume.4: Pension counts as money you keep. Only the deposit that earns a tax benefit is tried.
taxximizer.assume.5: Running costs are estimates; get quotes. Rates: taxtables.json ({note}).
taxximizer.disclaimer: Not tax advice. Moving an osek into a company (§104א), electing C-corp status or closing a file all have timing rules and costs of their own: decide with an Israeli CPA.
taxximizer.note.patur: No VAT charged or recovered. Turnover must stay under the ceiling; some professions can't be patur.
taxximizer.note.murshePlus: Charges VAT; can still take the 30% zair track under the ceiling.
taxximizer.note.murshe: Charges VAT, recovers input VAT, actual expenses.
taxximizer.note.ltd: 23% company tax, then salary and/or 30% dividend. From 2025 §62א(א1) can tax a one-person service company's profit as your salary once it has 750k accumulated profit or you hold other companies.
taxximizer.note.llc: Taxed in Israel as your own business income (actual expenses; §87ה blocks the zair 30%). No US tax without US-effectively-connected income. 5472 every year.
taxximizer.note.ccorp: 21% US tax, topped up to Israel's 23% because it's managed from Israel; dividends 25% US withholding credited against Israel's 30%. §75ב1 (foreign professional company) can tax programmers/consultants as if paid out.
